_README: S4's frozen expected-break fixture (acceptance.md:65, epics.md:836).
HAND-CHECKED ONCE AND THEN NEVER REGENERATED TO MAKE A TEST PASS.
There is no generator for this file, deliberately: nothing in this repository
can write it. `words` is the LABEL - the segmentation a reader would make - and
`expectedBreaks` is its arithmetic: the cumulative rune lengths of every word
but the last. Check the WORDS; the numbers follow. Positions are RUNE indices.
Every item is whitespace-free, so each break is zero-width and one position says
everything about it. `declaredAtomic: true` marks an item whose text is passed to
the engine as a DECLARED value (AD-25's third mechanism) rather than a bare
string - it is never split regardless of what a bare-string reading of the same
characters would propose.
THERE IS NO RULE THAT PREDICTS THESE LABELS, AND THAT IS THE POINT. An earlier
revision of this file claimed thai-003..thai-010 were corrected to one word each
'on evidence independent of the engine's output (headword membership in the
shipped wordlist)'. The owner's 2026-08-24 hand-check falsified that claim:
measured against the shipped wordlist, thai-007/008/009 are headwords, so are
their split constituents, and so are all five items kept whole (thai-003/004/
005/006/010) and their constituents too. Headword membership does not, and
cannot, distinguish the three the owner split from the five they kept. These
labels are per-item native-speaker judgments. No rule derivable from the shipped
wordlist predicts them - this is AD-25's stated impossibility (the engine never
infers dictionary membership; it cannot, per the Surname Act argument), observed
here from the acceptability side rather than the surname side. The fixture is
the oracle BECAUSE no rule can replace it.
THREE STATES, RECORDED SEPARATELY - SILENCE IS NOT RATIFICATION.
Explicitly corrected by the owner's 2026-08-24 hand-check: thai-007, thai-008,
thai-009 (split - the engine's conservative 'no break' was too narrow for what a
reader accepts), and cjk-004, cjk-005, cjk-007 (declared unbreakable - a bare-
string reading proposed breaks a reader rejects for these specific values).
Explicitly declined: none remain - cjk-005 was re-asked with its actual break
positions shown (see its gloss) and the owner changed the answer.
Unremarked, therefore NOT ratified: thai-003, thai-004, thai-005, thai-006,
thai-010 (student, school, hospital, train, receipt) - never raised in the
hand-check, so their 'kept whole' labels stand only as the Story 2.4 agent's
original judgment, not as anything the owner has confirmed.
AC14's exact-equality assertion has a small, enumerated, justified exception for
thai-007/008/009 - see TestS4ExpectedBreaksMatchTheEngine's s4ExpectedDivergences
in folio-go/internal/text/s4_expected_test.go. The engine cannot be made to
propose these breaks without inventing a heuristic (forbidden by AD-25) or
editing the shipped wordlist to make a real Thai word disappear (forbidden,
D-000.32) - the fixture stays the human oracle and the engine's conservative
shortfall is named and bounded instead of hidden inside a relaxed assertion.
